maria_sales: FYI — Orbis POC is failing on the embeddings->rerank step. They send a batch and get a 400 with a dims error. Can we SWARM? :eyes:
aj_engineer: Can you paste the exact error and the request payload (headers + body)?
maria_sales: Here are the logs Jordan sent (redacted client id):
```
POST /v1/rerank HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer xxxxx

{
  "query_embedding": [0.12, 0.03, ..., 0.44],
  "candidates": [[...], [...]],
  "model": "rerank-bert-large"
}

Response: 400 Bad Request
{
  "error": "embedding dimension mismatch: expected 1536, got 768"
}
```
tess_ml: That exact message means the reranker model expects 1536-dim vectors but the client is sending 768-dim ones. Most common causes: client is using older/smaller embedding model or they double-encoded / truncated vectors.
aj_engineer: @maria_sales do we know which embedding model the client used?
maria_sales: Jordan said their client lib calls "text-embed-ada-002" internally — we asked for full request but they were on a tight demo loop.

alex_se: Quick repro checklist: 1) Ask for the embedding model name + vector length in their payload. 2) Confirm server-side they didn't accidentally downsample / np.float16 round-trip. 3) Check batching logic: we sometimes see clients concat multiple vectors incorrectly.

maria_sales: They also observed occasional 413 Payload Too Large when they tried to send 6k candidates in a single call. So two problems: dims + batch size.
aj_engineer: For the payload size: large candidate lists should be chunked. Recommend batch <= 512 for rerank with large models, or use our streaming rerank endpoint (if they need to stream) — depends on candidate length. Also set content-encoding: gzip on client if supported.
tess_ml: On dims: workaround options while client fixes embedding model: 1) re-embed on our side — send raw text, use our embeddings model to encode server-side before rerank (we can autoconvert). 2) if they insist on using their vectors, they must produce 1536-dim vectors. We should not pad/truncate silently as it breaks semantics.

maria_sales: Jordan asked about cost if we re-embed server-side for POC. He also asked whether Dedicated would avoid rate limits.
sam_security: On Dedicated: yes, reserved capacity reduces rate throttling, but security/compliance review required for private data. We'll need a completed security questionnaire + SAML + contractual CLAs for customer-owned keys if they want KMS. I can DM the template.

alex_se: For immediate unblock: mari, can you ask Jordan to: 1) run a quick script to print len(embedding) for their embedding generator; 2) reduce candidate batch to 256 and retry; 3) attach a single failing payload (so we can inspect JSON encoding). Example snippet to run client-side:```python
vec = get_embedding(text)
print(len(vec))
```
If they get 768, that's our answer.
maria_sales: Pasted the snippet to them. Jordan ran it and confirmed len=768. He says their internal model is a legacy 768-dim model.
aj_engineer: OK, documented steps:
- Short-term POC options: A) Switch client to our recommended embedding model (1536) — fastest fix. B) Send raw text -> use server-side embed then rerank (we can enable for POC; note extra token costs). C) If they want us to map 768->1536, that's nontrivial (would require training a projection or padding which is likely to degrade quality).

alex_se: I'll draft a POC plan for Orbis: 1) Enable server-side embed option for rerank (flag we can toggle), 2) Set max candidates per call to 256 and recommend gzip, 3) Provide sample client patch and sample cURL.

maria_sales: Can you paste the cURL for server-side embedding option? Jordan's ops team wants something they can test quickly.
aj_engineer: cURL example:```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \\n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\n  -d '{"raw_documents": ["doc1 text", "doc2 text", ...], "query": "user query", "rerank_model": "rerank-bert-large", "embed_on_server": true, "max_candidates": 256}'
```
This instructs our backend to run embeddings with our standard 1536 model before rerank.

maria_sales: Jordan ran that and it moved past the dims error. Great. He reported slower response though (adds ~120ms per candidate batch) — he asked if there's a better perf config for POC.
tess_ml: For perf: enable prefix/KV cache (if queries are similar), reduce candidate size, and use a smaller reranker for POC (e.g., rerank-base instead of large) — accuracy tradeoff but much faster. Also consider using approximate prefiltering (cosine on embeddings, top-K 200 then rerank).

maria_sales: On pricing — Jordan asked if we can discount server-side embedding costs for POC and what Dedicated pricing looks like. I'm going to loop in finance but any quick guidance?
aj_engineer: For POC discounts we usually offer 50% off embedding tokens up to a cap for 30 days; Dedicated pricing is custom, depends on commit and latency SLOs. Sales should propose a POC credit and note that Dedicated removes noisy rate limits.

sam_security: Also flagged: Orbis wants us to sign an NDA and complete their infosec questionnaire. I'll send our SOC2 + pen test summary and the questionnaire link. Expect a 2-3 day turnaround on the security review for Dedicated.

alex_se: Next steps I can own: 1) Push a quick feature flag to enable embed_on_server for this org id (short-lived). 2) Provide sample client patch and recommended batch sizes. 3) Send a short doc on tradeoffs (dims, batching, costs).
maria_sales: Thanks all — Jordan will test the server-side embed flow and report performance numbers tomorrow. I'll also start the POC credit + security paperwork. :thumbsup:
